question:
I'm studying the effects of product safety legislation on safety recalls during periods of economic turmoil, with a main focus on the Covid-19 pandemic in Australia and gas products. 

Give me a list of the PRA Numbers of all product safety recalls posted on www.productsafety.gov.au between 1 January 2020 and 1 July 2020 (inclusive) that have been labelled as containing the topic "Gas products and appliances". Exclude products that were not sold 'Nationally'.

The list should look like this: 2020/11111, 2020/11112, 2020/11115, 2020/11116, 2020/11117, 2020/11119, 2020/11125

Reasoning: medium
Read pages for a research assistant and follow useful links recursively. During
extraction, only the supplied page is evidence. The question defines what to look
for; parent reasoning guides navigation but is not this page's evidence.

Preserve exact relevant names and rows with their headers, values, units, dates
and scope. Never replace relevant rows with ellipses, examples or instructions to
continue the list. If all rows cannot fit, prioritize rows useful to the question
and explicitly mark omissions. A partial, restricted or truncated list is not the
complete candidate set. Missing fields are unknown. Keep relevant discoveries even
if they answer a different part of the original question.

Follow links likely to fill a candidate's missing condition or reach the required
document/year. An index can be useful without answer facts. If content repeats,
try a detail page or another supported route. Links outside the menu and inferred
paths on an observed site are allowed. Child notes are returned automatically;
do not copy their facts into your own note. Retain useful unvisited links even
when expansion stops.

For extraction return:
**Final Information**
**Page:** Actual title and URL.
**Evidence:** Exact relevant facts/rows and short supporting quotes.
**Coverage:** Actual entities, years, population; full list, subset or excerpt.
**Missing:** Requested fields this page does not establish.
**Next links:** Useful URLs and the missing field each could establish.
**Expand:** yes or no, and why.
**Status:** partial
Use answered only if this page supplies all requested facts, partial for useful

**Original Question:**
I'm studying the effects of product safety legislation on safety recalls during periods of economic turmoil, with a main focus on the Covid-19 pandemic in Australia and gas products. 

Give me a list of the PRA Numbers of all product safety recalls posted on www.productsafety.gov.au between 1 January 2020 and 1 July 2020 (inclusive) that have been labelled as containing the topic "Gas products and appliances". Exclude products that were not sold 'Nationally'.

# Macpac Micro-Stove

Macpac NZ Ltd

### Recall published

29 June 2020

### Topics

[Gas products and appliances](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10043)

[Sports and recreation](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10087)

[Camping](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10089)

## Product description

A small, portable butane burner appliance that can screw onto a portable butane canister.   
  
 The product is designed with a screw thread for attachment and 3 folding legs on which to place a small cooking vessel such as a pot.   
  
 The product is for use when hiking or camping in the wilderness. 

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 6: Photograph of Macpac Micro-Stove](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Macpac%20Micro-Stove.jpg?itok=759ML2xL)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Macpac%20Micro-Stove.jpg?itok=v0wJUoJJ)

[![Image 7: Photograph of Underneath Macpac Micro-Stove](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Underneath%20Macpac%20Micro-Stove.jpg?itok=MtJAkfVt)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Underneath%20Macpac%20Micro-Stove.jpg?itok=9LaXIk2-)[![Image 8: Photograph of Macpac Micro-Stove Side](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Macpac%20Micro-Stove%20Side.jpg?itok=AKYdiBuQ)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Macpac%20Micro-Stove%20Side.jpg?itok=t1t4FOrK)[![Image 9: Photograph of Macpac Micro-Stove with Packaging](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Macpac%20Micro-Stove%20with%20Packaging.jpg?itok=HkbPaL8o)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Macpac%20Micro-Stove%20with%20Packaging.jpg?itok=ehhU_V1W)

## Reason the product is recalled

The product does not meet the required gas safety standard. The threaded component may be difficult to connect to the butane canister.  
  
  

## The hazards to consumers

Gas can leak for longer than the expected short burst when screwing the product onto the canister. If this occurs near an ignition source, the released flammable gas may ignite resulting in a fire or serious illness, injury or death.  
  

## What consumers should do

Customers must stop using the product immediately and return it to their nearest Macpac retail store for a full refund. In addition to a refund, Macpac is offering customers a $20 store voucher upon returning the product.  
  
 For further information, consumers can contact Macpac Australia on 1800 325 215 or email customerservice@macpac.com.au or go to https://www.macpac.com.au/product-recall.html

# Chant Gas Hose Assembly model A003 as attached to Jumbuck Stardom 4 Burner BBQ model HS884502

Pacific Gas & Heating Pty Ltd

### Recall published

10 March 2020

### Topics

[Gas products and appliances](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10043)

[Home and garden](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10044)

[Outdoor furniture and barbecues](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10057)

## Product description

Chant Gas Hose Assembly model number A003  
  
 As attached to Jumbuck Stardom 4 Burner BBQ model number HS-884502  
  
 All hose assemblies attached to a Jumbuck Stardom 4B BBQ, under the coverage of AGA certificate 8169G, with a manufacture year and month of 2019/06. The month of manufacture is stated on the data label located inside the cabinet door.  
  
 Sold through Bunnings Warehouse stores between 5 August 2019 and 23 January 2020

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 6: Photograph of Chant Gas Hose Assembly](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Chant%20Gas%20Hose%20Assembly.jpg?itok=tEH_yQf2)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Chant%20Gas%20Hose%20Assembly.jpg?itok=DJJ0pqMf)

## Reason the product is recalled

The last thread of the handwheel on the hose assembly may not be completely machined. A hose assembly with this fault will not seal correctly with an LPG cylinder and gas may leak from the connection point.

## The hazards to consumers

Risk of leaking gas at the connection with an LPG cylinder could lead to burns and/or a fire and/or explosion, which may result in serious injury.

## What consumers should do

Consumers should immediately turn off the gas supply and disconnect the hose assembly from the LPG cylinder.  
 Check the date of purchase and the month and year of manufacture of their BBQ. If in is range, do not use the BBQ and contact Pacific Gas & Heating on 1300 793 978 to receive instructions on how to disconnect the hose assembly from the BBQ.  
  
 Consumers can either:  
 1. Request that Pacific Gas & Heating mail a replacement hose assembly to their home address.  
 2. Take the hose assembly to any Bunnings store to receive a replacement hose assembly.   
  
 For further information, contact Pacific Gas & Heating on 1300 793 978 or email at info@pacificgas.com.au

# Chant Gas Hose Assembly model A003 as attached to Jumbuck Stardom 4 Burner BBQ model HS884502

Pacific Gas & Heating Pty Ltd

### Recall published

10 March 2020

### Topics

[Gas products and appliances](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10043)

[Home and garden](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10044)

[Outdoor furniture and barbecues](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10057)

## Product description

Chant Gas Hose Assembly model number A003  
  
 As attached to Jumbuck Stardom 4 Burner BBQ model number HS-884502  
  
 All hose assemblies attached to a Jumbuck Stardom 4B BBQ, under the coverage of AGA certificate 8169G, with a manufacture year and month of 2019/06. The month of manufacture is stated on the data label located inside the cabinet door.  
  
 Sold through Bunnings Warehouse stores between 5 August 2019 and 23 January 2020

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 6: Photograph of Chant Gas Hose Assembly](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Chant%20Gas%20Hose%20Assembly.jpg?itok=tEH_yQf2)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Chant%20Gas%20Hose%20Assembly.jpg?itok=DJJ0pqMf)

## Reason the product is recalled

The last thread of the handwheel on the hose assembly may not be completely machined. A hose assembly with this fault will not seal correctly with an LPG cylinder and gas may leak from the connection point.

## The hazards to consumers

Risk of leaking gas at the connection with an LPG cylinder could lead to burns and/or a fire and/or explosion, which may result in serious injury.

## What consumers should do

Consumers should immediately turn off the gas supply and disconnect the hose assembly from the LPG cylinder.  
 Check the date of purchase and the month and year of manufacture of their BBQ. If in is range, do not use the BBQ and contact Pacific Gas & Heating on 1300 793 978 to receive instructions on how to disconnect the hose assembly from the BBQ.  
  
 Consumers can either:  
 1. Request that Pacific Gas & Heating mail a replacement hose assembly to their home address.  
 2. Take the hose assembly to any Bunnings store to receive a replacement hose assembly.   
  
 For further information, contact Pacific Gas & Heating on 1300 793 978 or email at info@pacificgas.com.au

Jaha Holdings Pty Ltd

### Recall published

16 February 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

## Product description

Apache RTC1 Camper  
 Model Year 2019  
  
 16 affected camper vans

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 5: Photograph of Titan Apache RTC1 Camper](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Titan%20Apache%20RTC1%20Camper.jpg?itok=WkId2cnp)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Titan%20Apache%20RTC1%20Camper.jpg?itok=kzcWNDII)

## Reason the product is recalled

Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is a colourless, highly flammable gas that may leak and build up inside the camper.  
  
 The gas appliances have not been installed in accordance with the gas safety standard for installation in caravans and boats for non-propulsive purposes:  
  
 1. There is no gas escape hole installed for the cooker and refrigerator in accordance with the manufacturer's installation instructions.  
 2. The ventilation system for the refrigerator has not been installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s installation instructions.  

## The hazards to consumers

In the event of an LPG gas leak, unburnt gas could build up in the refrigerator rear cavity that could result in a fire, which could cause serious illness, injury or death.

## What consumers should do

Consumers should stop using all gas appliances immediately and contact the manufacturer and arrange for inspection/rectification of the gas installation.   
  
 For further information, consumers can contact the manufacturer Jaha Holdings Pty Ltd on   
 07 3888 0360 or email service@caravanrsc.com.au

## Product description

Apache RTC1 Camper  
 Model Year 2019  
  
 16 affected camper vans

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 5: Photograph of Titan Apache RTC1 Camper](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Titan%20Apache%20RTC1%20Camper.jpg?itok=WkId2cnp)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Titan%20Apache%20RTC1%20Camper.jpg?itok=kzcWNDII)

## Reason the product is recalled

Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is a colourless, highly flammable gas that may leak and build up inside the camper.  
  
 The gas appliances have not been installed in accordance with the gas safety standard for installation in caravans and boats for non-propulsive purposes:  
  
 1. There is no gas escape hole installed for the cooker and refrigerator in accordance with the manufacturer's installation instructions.  
 2. The ventilation system for the refrigerator has not been installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s installation instructions.  

## The hazards to consumers

In the event of an LPG gas leak, unburnt gas could build up in the refrigerator rear cavity that could result in a fire, which could cause serious illness, injury or death.

## What consumers should do

Consumers should stop using all gas appliances immediately and contact the manufacturer and arrange for inspection/rectification of the gas installation.   
  
 For further information, consumers can contact the manufacturer Jaha Holdings Pty Ltd on   
 07 3888 0360 or email service@caravanrsc.com.au

# Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve and Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve with Hose and Regulator

Mayo Hardware

### Recall published

18 August 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

## Product description

Grillman Gas safety shut off valve with POL fitting (sold with or without hose and regulator). Suitable for gas barbecues and outdoor gas heaters.   

### Brand

Grillman

See a list of details to help identify the product

## Reason the product is recalled

The tail pipe and main body of the valve may come apart. This may cause the seal at this point to break and allow gas to escape when the valve to the gas cylinder is open. The defect is only in the valve. The hose and regulator are not affected.  
  

## The hazards to consumers

Risk of leaking gas igniting, leading to burns and/or a fire and/or explosion, which may result in serious injury or death.  
  

## What consumers should do

Consumers should immediately stop using the products and return them to the place of purchase for a full refund.  
  
 For further information, contact Mayo Hardware on 1300 360 211 or email grillmangas@mayohardware.com.au

# Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve and Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve with Hose and Regulator

Mayo Hardware

### Recall published

18 August 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

## Product description

Grillman Gas safety shut off valve with POL fitting (sold with or without hose and regulator). Suitable for gas barbecues and outdoor gas heaters.   

### Brand

Grillman

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 5: Photograph of GMGSG Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/GMGSG%20Grillman%20Gas%20Safety%20Shut%20Off%20Valve.jpg?itok=EJEAjf0h)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/GMGSG%20Grillman%20Gas%20Safety%20Shut%20Off%20Valve.jpg?itok=qisLeEQe)

[![Image 6: Photograph of Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve and Regulator GMGSGREG](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Grillman%20Gas%20Safety%20Shut%20Off%20Valve%20and%20Regulator%20GMGSGREG.jpg?itok=-FLcsIAl)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Grillman%20Gas%20Safety%20Shut%20Off%20Valve%20and%20Regulator%20GMGSGREG.jpg?itok=Z59sZrqg)[![Image 7: Photograph of identifying number 2018_01](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Identifying%20number%202018_01.jpg?itok=ye9J0SvE)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Identifying%20number%202018_01.jpg?itok=gjVYbs3u)[![Image 8: Photograph of Identifying number 2018_03](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Identifying%20number%202018_03.jpg?itok=eFSUU5xZ)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Identifying%20number%202018_03.jpg?itok=3fgiSu8E)

## Reason the product is recalled

The tail pipe and main body of the valve may come apart. This may cause the seal at this point to break and allow gas to escape when the valve to the gas cylinder is open. The defect is only in the valve. The hose and regulator are not affected.  
  

## The hazards to consumers

Risk of leaking gas igniting, leading to burns and/or a fire and/or explosion, which may result in serious injury or death.  
  

## What consumers should do

Consumers should immediately stop using the products and return them to the place of purchase for a full refund.  
  
 For further information, contact Mayo Hardware on 1300 360 211 or email grillmangas@mayohardware.com.au

# Millard Slide On Caravans

Bilsen GMW Pty Ltd

### Recall published

8 March 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

[Vehicle accessories (registered)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10104)

[Caravan, motorhome and camper accessories](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10107)

## Product description

Millard Slide On Caravan

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 6: Photograph of Millard Slide On Caravan](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Millard%20Slide%20On%20Caravan.png?itok=xb1FsayC)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Millard%20Slide%20On%20Caravan.png?itok=QNpC9tzU)

## Reason the product is recalled

Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is a colourless, highly flammable gas that may leak and build up inside the caravan as the consumer gas piping is located inside the caravan.  
  
 The consumer gas piping has not been installed in accordance with the relevant gas safety standard for installation in caravans for non-propulsive purposes.

## The hazards to consumers

In the event of an LPG gas leak, gas may accumulate within the caravan and may present a risk of poisoning or a fire, which could cause serious illness, injury or death.

## What consumers should do

Consumers should stop using gas in their caravan and contact an authorised Millard Caravan Dealer to arrange for the gas piping to be rerouted, free of charge.   
  
 To locate an authorised dealer, visit http://www.millardrv.com.au/dealers.aspx  
  
 For further information, consumers can contact Millard Caravans on 02 9829 2055 or http://www.millardrv.com.au/contact.aspx

### Recall published

### Topics

## Product description

Millard Slide On Caravan

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 6: Photograph of Millard Slide On Caravan](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Millard%20Slide%20On%20Caravan.png?itok=xb1FsayC)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Millard%20Slide%20On%20Caravan.png?itok=QNpC9tzU)

## Reason the product is recalled

Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is a colourless, highly flammable gas that may leak and build up inside the caravan as the consumer gas piping is located inside the caravan.  
  
 The consumer gas piping has not been installed in accordance with the relevant gas safety standard for installation in caravans for non-propulsive purposes.

## The hazards to consumers

In the event of an LPG gas leak, gas may accumulate within the caravan and may present a risk of poisoning or a fire, which could cause serious illness, injury or death.

## What consumers should do

Consumers should stop using gas in their caravan and contact an authorised Millard Caravan Dealer to arrange for the gas piping to be rerouted, free of charge.   
  
 To locate an authorised dealer, visit http://www.millardrv.com.au/dealers.aspx  
  
 For further information, consumers can contact Millard Caravans on 02 9829 2055 or http://www.millardrv.com.au/contact.aspx
